title: Temporal Invariance Is an Illusion: Time-Dependent Influences of the Galactic Magnetic Field on UHECR Observations
comment: 13 pages, 8 figures excl. appendix, or 18 pages, 12 figures incl. appendix
summary: Understanding the origin of the Ultra-High-Energy Cosmic Rays (UHECRs) requires explaining the features of their energy spectrum, mass composition, and arrival directions. Current modeling approaches neglect the time evolution of UHECR observables, a factor that is particularly important in the case of bursting UHECR sources. This study focuses on the influence of time delays caused by the galactic magnetic field (GMF) on the spectrum and arrival directions of UHECRs observed on Earth. Using CRPropa 3.2, we investigate the rigidity-dependence of the residence time of extragalactic cosmic rays entering our Galaxy. We find that UHECRs entering the Milky Way can experience delays of hundreds of kiloyears relative to light, and we demonstrate that these delays significantly alter the UHECR observables. Notably, a cutoff emerges in the transient scenario within the rigidity range of $10^{18}-10^{19}$ V, which coincides with the spectral break observed in data. We find a progressive shift in composition favoring heavier nuclei, as well as a delay distribution that is correlated with GMF strength. This causes the particles to be less correlated with their initial direction the larger their delays. A dipole-like anisotropy develops over timescales of about $\sim$100 kyr in certain bursts scenarios. Our results provide an alternative explanation for the UHECR spectral cutoff that does not invoke limits on source acceleration. This could potentially revise existing constraints.

AI.tldr: This paper uses CRPropa 3.2 simulations to show that galactic magnetic field delays (hundreds of kiloyears) significantly alter UHECR observables in transient source scenarios, producing a spectral cutoff at 10^18-10^19 V, composition shift toward heavier nuclei, and dipole anisotropy, offering an alternative explanation for the UHECR spectral cutoff without invoking source acceleration limits.
AI.motivation: Current UHECR modeling approaches neglect time evolution of observables, particularly important for bursting sources. Understanding the origin of UHECRs requires explaining features of their energy spectrum, mass composition, and arrival directions.
AI.method: Using CRPropa 3.2 simulations, the study investigates rigidity-dependent residence time delays of extragalactic cosmic rays entering the Milky Way, caused by the galactic magnetic field (GMF).
AI.result: UHECRs experience delays of hundreds of kiloyears relative to light. A cutoff emerges in the transient scenario at rigidity 10^18-10^19 V, matching observed spectral break. Composition shifts progressively toward heavier nuclei. Delay distribution correlates with GMF strength, reducing directional correlation. Dipole anisotropy develops over ~100 kyr timescales in some burst scenarios.
AI.conclusion: GMF-induced delays provide an alternative explanation for the UHECR spectral cutoff that does not require invoking limits on source acceleration, potentially revising existing constraints.

title: Predictions for the X-ray polarisation modulation in Cygnus X-1 from reflection off the stellar companion and its wind
summary: Context. Cyg X-1 is one of the brightest X-ray binaries and has been observed multiple times with the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE). Recent studies report tentative evidence for a polarisation modulation with the orbital period P, but a half-period (P/2) signal, expected from reflection off the companion star and its stellar wind, has not been reported. Aims. We aim to quantify the reflection-induced variations of the polarisation degree PD and polarisation angle PA in Cyg X-1 as a function of orbital phase and energy, and interpret these in terms of binary geometry and wind structure. Methods. We set up a radiative transfer model combining a general relativistic description of the polarised source emission (kerrC) with a focussed stellar wind model for the binary medium. Using the 3D X-ray radiative transfer code SKIRT, we simulate broadband Stokes I, Q, and U fluxes, surface brightness maps, and linear polarisation maps over one binary orbit. Results. We find a prominent double-peaked (P/2) polarisation modulation, with a peak-to-peak PD amplitude of 0.25, 0.81, and 1.24 percentage points in the 2-4, 4-6, and 6-8 keV bands, respectively, with a strong energy dependence. The PA modulation is more modest, with |ΔPA| < 4.6°. Crucially, X-ray reprocessing reduces the overall PD relative to the source polarisation. Conclusions. The modulation is driven by reflection off the companion star and the focussed wind, which induces a polarisation signal that alternately reinforces and counteracts the source polarisation throughout the orbit. The diffuse scattering halo surrounding the source systematically reduces the PD, an effect that should be accounted for in all wind-fed XRBs. The PD amplitude increases with energy as absorption disproportionately attenuates the distant-reflection signal; as the extinction drops, the reflection signal becomes increasingly important.

AI.tldr: This study models reprocessed X-ray polarization from Cygnus X-1 using radiative transfer, finding a half-orbit (P/2) modulation of polarization degree (up to 1.24 pp at 6-8 keV) driven by reflection off the companion star and focused wind, with diffuse scattering reducing overall polarization.
AI.motivation: To quantify reflection-induced polarization variations in Cyg X-1 as a function of orbital phase and energy, and interpret them in terms of binary geometry and wind structure, particularly because a half-period (P/2) signal expected from reflection has not been reported observationally.
AI.method: A radiative transfer model combining a general relativistic description of polarized source emission (kerrC) with a focused stellar wind model, using the 3D X-ray radiative transfer code SKIRT to simulate broadband Stokes I, Q, U fluxes, surface brightness maps, and linear polarization maps over one binary orbit.
AI.result: Found a double-peaked (P/2) polarization modulation with peak-to-peak PD amplitude of 0.25, 0.81, and 1.24 percentage points in the 2-4, 4-6, and 6-8 keV bands respectively, with strong energy dependence. PA modulation is modest (|ΔPA| < 4.6°). X-ray reprocessing reduces overall PD relative to source polarization.
AI.conclusion: The modulation arises from reflection off the companion star and focused wind, alternately reinforcing and counteracting source polarization. The diffuse scattering halo systematically reduces PD, an effect important for all wind-fed XRBs. PD amplitude increases with energy as absorption disproportionately attenuates the distant reflection signal.

title: The role of major mergers in triggering super-Eddington accretion
summary: JWST observations have opened a new era in the exploration of the high-redshift Universe, revealing black holes (BHs) with masses of several million solar masses already at $z>8$, challenging our understanding of their growth mechanisms. In this context, super-Eddington (SE) accretion has emerged as a promising solution and has been widely adopted in both numerical simulations and semi-analytical models. In this work, we investigate whether a major merger between two relatively low-mass halos ($M_{\rm halo}\sim10^9\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$) at high redshift can trigger episodes of sustained SE accretion, with particular focus on the role of BH feedback. We employ state-of-the-art, high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations of a major merger at $z\sim11$. We explore different prescriptions for BH seeding and feedback, including physically motivated radiative and kinetic models (winds and jets) across the three main accretion regimes: advection-dominated accretion flows (ADAF), radiatively efficient sub-Eddington accretion, and SE accretion. For the relatively low-mass halos studied here, our feedback prescription efficiently suppresses gas accretion, preventing substantial BH growth. We find that, although the merger drives gas inflows towards the central regions, this is not sufficient to trigger sustained SE accretion. Post-merger SE accretion episodes are observed only when BH feedback is entirely switched off. Amongst the feedback channels considered, kinetic feedback is the primary mechanism regulating BH growth. Moreover, the only significant SE accretion episodes occur immediately after BH seeding, while the merger itself does not produce a substantial enhancement of the accretion rate.

AI.tldr: This study uses high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations of a major merger at z~11 to test whether super-Eddington accretion can be triggered in low-mass halos (~10^9 M☉). The authors find that BH feedback—especially kinetic feedback—efficiently suppresses gas accretion, preventing sustained super-Eddington accretion unless feedback is entirely switched off. The merger itself does not significantly enhance accretion rates beyond the brief post-seeding period.
AI.motivation: JWST has discovered massive black holes (millions of solar masses) at z>8, challenging standard growth models. Super-Eddington accretion offers a potential resolution, but its feasibility in realistic merger-driven scenarios with BH feedback remains unclear. This work investigates whether major mergers at high redshift can actually trigger such sustained SE accretion.
AI.method: State-of-the-art, high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations of a major merger at z~11, with various BH seeding and feedback prescriptions (radiative, kinetic winds/jets) across three accretion regimes: ADAF, radiatively efficient sub-Eddington, and super-Eddington.
AI.result: BH feedback efficiently suppresses gas accretion in low-mass halos, preventing sustained SE accretion. Kinetic feedback is the dominant regulator. Only when feedback is entirely disabled does post-merger SE accretion occur. The only significant SE episodes happen immediately after BH seeding, not from the merger itself.
AI.conclusion: Mergers alone are insufficient to trigger sustained super-Eddington accretion in low-mass high-redshift halos; BH feedback (particularly kinetic modes) effectively curbs BH growth, challenging the idea that SE accretion easily resolves the tension with JWST-observed massive BHs at high redshift.

title: Periodic Radio and X-ray Emission from an Accreting White Dwarf Binary
summary: Long period radio transients (LPTs) are coherent bursts of polarised radio emission that repeat periodically on timescales of minutes to hours. Little is known about the physical origins of these systems. Astronomers have proposed magnetars that rotate slowly and white dwarfs that rapidly orbit with a companion star as potential explanations. While several recent examples appear to support the latter hypothesis, the mechanism generating these bright radio pulses remains poorly understood. Here we report our discovery and classification of the LPT ASKAP J174508.9-505149 as an accreting white dwarf binary. This object has a ~1.3h spectroscopic orbital period and exhibits orbitally-modulated X-ray emission and radio bursts. These elliptically polarised radio bursts drift in emission frequency, potentially due to a longer beat period, and turn off for several hours at a time. Some long period radio transients have been associated with non-interacting white dwarf binaries. We have spectroscopically confirmed this system as an accreting cataclysmic variable, identified through characteristic optical emission lines and an ongoing X-ray outburst. Our results strengthen the link between at least some long period radio transients and white dwarf binaries.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the discovery and classification of the long period radio transient (LPT) ASKAP J174508.9-505149 as an accreting white dwarf binary (cataclysmic variable), with a ~1.3h orbital period, orbitally-modulated X-ray emission, drifting elliptically polarised radio bursts, and spectroscopic confirmation via optical emission lines and an ongoing X-ray outburst, strengthening the link between LPTs and white dwarf binaries.
AI.motivation: Little is known about the physical origins of long period radio transients (LPTs), which are coherent bursts of polarised radio emission repeating on timescales of minutes to hours. While magnetars and white dwarf binaries have been proposed, the mechanism generating these bright radio pulses remains poorly understood.
AI.method: The authors discovered and classified the LPT ASKAP J174508.9-505149 through spectroscopic orbital period measurement (~1.3h), X-ray emission analysis showing orbital modulation, radio burst characterisation (elliptically polarised, frequency-drifting, intermittently turning off), and spectroscopic identification of characteristic optical emission lines confirming it as an accreting cataclysmic variable.
AI.result: ASKAP J174508.9-505149 is confirmed as an accreting white dwarf binary (cataclysmic variable) with a ~1.3h orbital period, orbitally-modulated X-ray emission, and elliptically polarised radio bursts that drift in frequency and turn off for several hours. An ongoing X-ray outburst was also detected.
AI.conclusion: This result strengthens the link between at least some long period radio transients and white dwarf binaries, providing direct spectroscopic confirmation of an accreting system among LPTs.

title: Studying the absorption signatures of H I Lyman-α in the warm-hot circumgalactic medium with TNG50
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A)
summary: In this study, we investigate the spectral signatures of neutral hydrogen Lyman-$α$ absorption arising from the warm-hot gas component of the circumgalactic medium (CGM) around $z=0$ Milky Way (MW)-like galaxies using the high-resolution TNG50 cosmological simulation. We used synthetic absorption spectra to identify and characterise coronal broad Ly$α$ absorbers (CBLAs), which represent H I absorption features produced by the warm-hot CGM at temperatures above $10^5$ K. Our study implies that CBLAs have a significant absorption cross-section, $f_c$, around MW-like galaxies. Based on an analysis of 75 sightlines intersecting the CGM of 15 galaxies in the mass range $10^{11.7} M_{\odot} \leq M_{200} \leq 10^{12.3} M_{\odot}$, we find $f_c \approx 0.8$ for $\log N_{\rm HI} \geq 13$, where CBLAs span a total column-density range $\log N_{\rm HI}=11.6-15.4$. Therefore, CBLAs provide a significant contribution to the overall H I optical depth in the CGM with $\sim 50\%$ of the CGM absorbers being dominated by CBLA absorption. Furthermore, we find that CBLAs trace warm-hot gas in a temperature range $T=10^{5.2-6.4}$ K, which accounts for $\sim 7\%$ of the overall baryon budget in the TNG50 galaxies and $\sim 25\%$ of the total CGM mass. Finally, we identify a population of strong CBLAs that exhibit substantial H I column densities up to $\log N_{\rm HI}=14.9$. This population represents a new absorber class tracing massive warm-hot circumgalactic structures at large radial distances. In conclusion, our study demonstrates that CBLAs represent an important absorber class that needs to be considered when interpreting the H I absorption signatures from the multi-phase CGM of MW-like galaxies at low redshift.

AI.tldr: Using TNG50 simulations, the authors identify and characterize coronal broad Lyα absorbers (CBLAs) from warm-hot CGM gas (T > 10⁵ K) around Milky Way-like galaxies at z=0, finding they have a large absorption cross-section (~0.8), contribute ~50% of H I optical depth in the CGM, account for ~25% of total CGM mass, and include a strong population tracing massive warm-hot structures at large radii.
AI.motivation: To investigate the spectral signatures of neutral hydrogen Lyman-α absorption from the warm-hot gas component of the circumgalactic medium (CGM) around Milky Way-like galaxies at z=0, and to characterize coronal broad Lyα absorbers (CBLAs) as a distinct absorber class.
AI.method: Analysis of synthetic absorption spectra from the high-resolution TNG50 cosmological simulation, examining 75 sightlines intersecting the CGM of 15 galaxies in the mass range 10¹¹.⁷ M⊙ ≤ M₂₀₀ ≤ 10¹².³ M⊙ to identify and characterize CBLAs.
AI.result: CBLAs have a significant absorption cross-section fc ≈ 0.8 for log N_HI ≥ 13, span column densities log N_HI = 11.6-15.4, contribute ~50% of overall H I optical depth in the CGM, trace warm-hot gas at T = 10⁵.²⁻⁶.⁴ K accounting for ~7% of total baryon budget and ~25% of CGM mass, and include strong CBLAs with log N_HI up to 14.9.
AI.conclusion: CBLAs represent an important absorber class that must be considered when interpreting H I absorption signatures from the multi-phase CGM of Milky Way-like galaxies at low redshift.

title: Earliest simultaneous multi-color optical observations of GRB 230328B: from 41 seconds to the host-galaxy identification
summary: We present a multi-wavelength analysis of the long-duration gamma-ray burst GRB 230328B. Fermi/GBM observations reveal a typical Type II burst with a duration of about 22 s. Using a photometric redshift of about 1.5 derived from the host galaxy, we find that the burst energetics, with an isotropic-equivalent energy of about 6.4*10^52 erg, are consistent with established empirical correlations for long gamma-ray bursts. The optical, X-ray, and radio afterglow exhibits a complex temporal evolution, featuring an early onset bump followed by a pronounced late-time achromatic rebrightening at about 4000 s. Through MCMC modeling, we find that the afterglow can be explained by forward shock emission with late energy injection. Broadband spectral energy distribution fitting reveals significant line-of-sight dust extinction, corresponding to a visual extinction of about 0.8 magnitudes, consistent with Milky Way or Large Magellanic Cloud dust properties. The burst originated in a relatively young, highly absorbed S0-type host galaxy, whose morphological analysis suggests that it may be part of a system of interacting galaxies. Finally, late-time optical monitoring reveals no signature of an accompanying supernova.

AI.tldr: GRB 230328B is a long-duration Type II gamma-ray burst at z~1.5 with isotropic-equivalent energy ~6.4×10^52 erg. Its afterglow shows complex evolution with an early bump and late achromatic rebrightening at ~4000 s, modeled by forward shock emission with late energy injection. Significant dust extinction (A_V ~ 0.8 mag) is present in its young, highly absorbed S0-type host galaxy, possibly part of an interacting system. No associated supernova is detected.
AI.motivation: To characterize the multi-wavelength properties (gamma-ray, X-ray, optical, radio) of GRB 230328B, constrain its progenitor environment, and test its consistency with known GRB correlations and emission mechanisms.
AI.method: Multi-wavelength observations including Fermi/GBM, optical, X-ray, and radio afterglow monitoring; photometric redshift from host galaxy; MCMC forward shock modeling with late energy injection; broadband SED fitting for dust extinction; host galaxy morphological analysis.
AI.result: GRB 230328B is a typical Type II burst with E_iso ~ 6.4×10^52 erg consistent with known correlations. The afterglow exhibits complex temporal evolution including a late achromatic rebrightening at ~4000 s, well explained by forward shock + late energy injection. Visual extinction A_V ~ 0.8 mag is found. The host is a young, dusty S0-type galaxy, possibly interacting. No supernova component is detected.
AI.conclusion: GRB 230328B fits within the long GRB population energetically and temporally, with its complex afterglow requiring late energy injection. The host environment is significantly obscured and relatively young, consistent with an interacting galaxy system. The absence of an associated supernova leaves uncertain the nature of the progenitor.

title: Simulating realistic radio morphologies of Fanaroff-Riley I jets in a self-regulating cool-core cluster
summary: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) jets radiate radio synchrotron emission displaying a wide range of morphologies. At the same time, they provide heat to prevent cooling flows in cool-core galaxy clusters. We produce mock radio observations of AGN jets in a self-regulating cool-core galaxy cluster. To this end, we employ magneto-hydrodynamical simulations of an idealised Perseus-like galaxy cluster, in which accretion-powered low-density jets accelerate cosmic ray protons and electrons by means of a sub-grid model. Cosmic ray electron spectra are spatially and temporally evolved along Lagrangian tracer trajectories using the Fokker-Planck solver Crest to produce radio synchrotron emission. Self-regulated AGN jets stabilize the cool-core cluster against cooling flows and produce realistic Fanaroff-Riley I (FRI) and disturbed lobe morphologies, in contrast to symmetrical lobe structures obtained with a single jet outburst of fixed power. Our mock radio observations are viewed in a blazar configuration - along the jet axis - and exhibit complex radio-emitting lobe structures despite this. This highlights the strong deflection of light jets by cold gas structures and suggests that small-scale black hole and jet properties cannot be inferred from kpc-scale FRI radio lobe morphologies. Combining self-consistently evolved magnetic fields and electron spectra enables us to explain a known observational phenomenon, whereby radio observations of AGN lobes on galaxy cluster scales occasionally display similar spatial extents at different frequencies: in 1-50 $μ$G magnetic fields obtained in our cool-core environment, both freshly accelerated and hundreds-of-Myr-old electrons are able to contribute to the 150 MHz - 1.4 GHz frequency range.

AI.tldr: This study uses magneto-hydrodynamical simulations of a Perseus-like cool-core galaxy cluster with self-regulating AGN jets to produce mock radio observations. The simulations show that self-regulated jets produce realistic FRI and disturbed lobe morphologies (unlike symmetric lobes from single outbursts), and that complex lobe structures persist even in blazar viewing configurations due to jet deflection by cold gas. The work explains why radio observations at different frequencies (150 MHz–1.4 GHz) sometimes show similar spatial extents, as both fresh and aged electrons can contribute across this range in the typical 1–50 μG magnetic fields of cool-core environments.
AI.motivation: To understand how AGN jets self-regulate cooling flows in cool-core galaxy clusters and to produce realistic mock radio observations that can explain observed morphologies and spectral behaviors.
AI.method: Magneto-hydrodynamical simulations of an idealized Perseus-like cluster with accretion-powered low-density jets; cosmic ray electron spectra evolved along Lagrangian tracers using the Fokker-Planck solver Crest; mock radio synchrotron emission generated from the simulations.
AI.result: Self-regulated AGN jets produce realistic FRI and disturbed lobe morphologies (vs. symmetric lobes from a single outburst). Complex structures persist even in blazar viewing geometry due to jet deflection by cold gas. The 1–50 μG magnetic fields allow both freshly accelerated and hundreds-of-Myr-old electrons to contribute to 150 MHz–1.4 GHz emission, explaining observed similar spatial extents across frequencies.
AI.conclusion: Small-scale black hole and jet properties cannot be inferred from kpc-scale FRI radio lobe morphologies. Self-consistent magnetic field and electron spectra evolution can explain observed frequency-dependent spatial extents in AGN lobes.

title: NICER detection of a new candidate cyclotron line in the bursting X-ray pulsar GRO J1744-28
comment: 9 pages, 10 figures, and 4 tables. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: We report the detection of cyclotron resonant scattering features (CRSFs) in the spectrum of the unique bursting pulsar GRO J1744-28, observed during its recent outburst in 2021 with the Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer (NICER). Clear pulsations at a frequency of 2.141128 Hz as well as Type II X-ray bursts were observed. The pulse profile exhibits a single-peaked shape in all energy bands, with the pulse fraction showing a positive correlation with energy. We find that the persistent X-ray continuum of the accreting pulsar is well described by typical phenomenological models, and we confirm the presence of the cyclotron line at $\sim$5 keV as reported in previous studies. In addition, we detect a candidate absorption feature with a centroid energy of 2 keV. If confirmed, this feature could be interpreted as a CRSF, which would correspond to a magnetic field of $\sim$1.8 $\times 10^{11}$ G. Pulse-phase-resolved analysis also reveals this absorption line around the peak pulse phases. These NICER observations provide tentative evidence for the cyclotron line candidate, establishing GRO J1744-28 as a key laboratory for studying accretion physics in an intermediate-strength magnetic field.

AI.tldr: NICER observations of the bursting pulsar GRO J1744-28 during its 2021 outburst confirm a cyclotron line at ~5 keV and detect a candidate 2 keV absorption feature (possibly a CRSF corresponding to ~1.8×10¹¹ G magnetic field), with pulse-phase-resolved analysis supporting the candidate line around peak phases.
AI.motivation: To study the unique bursting pulsar GRO J1744-28 using NICER observations from its 2021 outburst, investigating its timing properties, continuum emission, and cyclotron resonant scattering features to understand accretion physics in intermediate-strength magnetic fields.
AI.method: Timing analysis (2.141128 Hz pulsations detected), phenomenological continuum modeling, detection of cyclotron lines via spectral fitting (confirmed ~5 keV line, candidate ~2 keV feature), and pulse-phase-resolved spectroscopy.
AI.result: Confirmed the ~5 keV cyclotron line; detected a candidate 2 keV absorption feature potentially corresponding to B ~ 1.8×10¹¹ G; single-peaked pulse profile with positive energy-pulse fraction correlation; Type II X-ray bursts observed.
AI.conclusion: GRO J1744-28 serves as a key laboratory for accreting pulsar physics with intermediate magnetic field strength, with tentative evidence for a second cyclotron line candidate at 2 keV.

title: Ceci n'est pas une Couche de Mélange: The Meaning of Resolved Turbulent Radiative Mixing
summary: Turbulent Radiative Mixing Layers (TRMLs) are of fundamental importance to the transport of energy and momentum in multi-phase, astrophysical fluids. We use measurements of the "micro" and "macro" properties of these layers in high-resolution \texttt{AthenaK} simulations to investigate when their properties can be considered \textit{well}-resolved. In particular, we demonstrate that the previously noticed resolution independence of total cooling, $\dot{E}_{\rm cool}$, in these simulations is due to a remarkable, and perhaps fortuitous, cancellation of the countervailing effects of numerical dissipation and numerical viscosity. This calls into question the degree to which we can trust the results of these experiments, as there is no physical picture that explains this cancellation. We also demonstrate that in order to correctly resolve the phase structure in these layers, important for accurate predictions of their observable properties, one must resolve the scale on which turbulent diffusion acts on time-scales comparable to the cooling time. This "turbulent Field length", $λ_{\rm F,turb}$, is where the eddy turnover time is equal to the cooling time ($t_{\rm eddy}(λ_{\rm F,turb}) = t_{\rm cool}$). We demonstrate that resolving this scale results in converged phase-structure and spatially resolved transitions in the gas phases.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates resolution requirements for Turbulent Radiative Mixing Layers (TRMLs) in astrophysical fluids, finding that previously observed resolution independence of total cooling is due to cancellation of numerical dissipation and viscosity effects, and introducing the "turbulent Field length" scale ($\lambda_{\rm F,turb}$) as a necessary resolution criterion for properly capturing phase structure.
AI.motivation: TRMLs are fundamental to energy and momentum transport in multi-phase astrophysical fluids, but the reliability of simulation results had been called into question due to poorly understood resolution independence of key quantities like total cooling rate.
AI.method: High-resolution AthenaK simulations measuring micro and macro properties of TRMLs, analyzing resolution dependence of cooling rates and phase structure convergence.
AI.result: The resolution independence of $\dot{E}_{\rm cool}$ results from a cancellation between numerical dissipation and numerical viscosity effects, with no physical explanation. Proper phase-structure resolution requires resolving the "turbulent Field length" where $t_{\rm eddy} = t_{\rm cool}$.
AI.conclusion: Resolving $\lambda_{\rm F,turb}$ yields converged phase-structure and spatially resolved gas phase transitions, providing a physically motivated resolution criterion for TRML simulations.

title: A candidate cyclotron line at 1.89 keV in the ultraluminous X-ray source NGC 4861 X-2
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics Letters
summary: In this Letter, we report the detection of an absorption-like feature at ~1.89 keV in Chandra/ACIS spectra of the ultraluminous X-ray source NGC 4861 X-2, based on the deepest observation (ObsID 20992; ~58 ks). The feature is consistently recovered across independent continuum models and significantly improves the fit statistics. Monte Carlo simulations yield a detection significance of ~3.5-4.1 sigma, depending on the adopted continuum, and a blind line scan reveals a single, localized peak at the same energy. The observed properties are consistent with a proton cyclotron resonant scattering feature (CRSF), implying a magnetic field strength of B ~(3-4) x 10^14 G. The spectrum is well described by a multicolor disk blackbody (diskbb) with kTin ~0.8 keV or a strongly curved continuum with a low cutoff energy (cutoffpl; Ecut ~1.3 keV). The source shows variability confined to the soft X-ray band in the two Chandra observations where the absorption-like feature is detected. In these observations, a candidate periodic signal at P ~7.4 s is also detected, with a global significance of ~2.5 sigma.

AI.tldr: Detection of a ~1.89 keV absorption feature in NGC 4861 X-2, interpreted as a proton cyclotron resonant scattering feature (CRSF) implying B ~(3-4)×10^14 G, along with a candidate ~7.4 s periodic signal.
AI.motivation: To report and characterize an absorption-like feature at ~1.89 keV in the deepest Chandra/ACIS observation of the ultraluminous X-ray source NGC 4861 X-2, and to determine its physical origin.
AI.method: Analysis of Chandra/ACIS spectra (ObsID 20992; ~58 ks) with independent continuum models, Monte Carlo simulations for significance assessment, blind line scan, and timing analysis.
AI.result: A ~1.89 keV absorption feature detected at ~3.5-4.1σ significance, consistent with a proton CRSF implying B ~(3-4)×10^14 G. Soft-band variability and a candidate P ~7.4 s period signal (~2.5σ) also found.
AI.conclusion: The absorption feature likely represents a proton cyclotron line from a strongly magnetized neutron star, supporting the neutron star interpretation of ultraluminous X-ray sources.

title: Mapping the nuclear environments of extreme coronal line emitting galaxies
summary: Extreme coronal line emitters (ECLEs) are a rare class of galactic nuclei exhibiting unusually strong high-ionisation forbidden emission lines, and several ECLEs have been linked to tidal disruption events (TDEs). In this work, we compile and analyse optical spectra of 33 ECLEs, dividing them into variable, TDE-linked sources and non-variable, AGN-linked systems. Using multi-epoch spectroscopy from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey, Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, and other facilities, we investigate the evolution of the emission line spectra and measure emission line profiles. Many variable ECLEs have changing spectra in which the highest-ionisation lines (e.g., [Fe X]-[Fe XIV]) appear and fade first, followed by [Fe VII], accompanied by brightening of [O III]. These changes may reflect a softening ionising continuum, the outward propagation of the ionisation front following the TDE flare, or both. Assuming virial motion, we translate line widths into characteristic radial distances, reconstructing the spatial distribution of line-emitting gas. Coronal lines are generally emitted at radii intermediate between the broad line region and the low-ionisation narrow line region. This ionisation stratification is seen in many sources, with similar incidence in variable and non-variable ECLEs, suggesting no apparent difference in circumnuclear gas distributions between active and quiescent nuclei. We find positive correlations between gas distance and black hole mass for both [O III] and [Fe VII]: the log(Distance)-log(Mass) relations have slopes $0.63\pm0.08$ and $0.69\pm0.12$, respectively, broadly consistent with a Mass$^{0.5}$ dependence and with characteristic radii set primarily by photoionisation.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes optical spectra of 33 extreme coronal line emitters (ECLEs), classifying them into variable (TDE-linked) and non-variable (AGN-linked) sources. Using multi-epoch spectroscopy, they find that variable ECLEs show temporal evolution where high-ionisation coronal lines fade first, followed by lower-ionisation lines, indicating a softening ionising continuum or propagating ionisation fronts. The study reconstructs the spatial distribution of line-emitting gas, showing coronal lines originate at intermediate radii between broad and narrow line regions. Positive correlations between gas distance and black hole mass are found for [O III] and [Fe VII], with slopes consistent with a Mass^0.5 dependence.
AI.motivation: To understand the nature of extreme coronal line emitters (ECLEs), which are rare galactic nuclei exhibiting unusually strong high-ionisation forbidden lines, and to determine whether they are primarily linked to tidal disruption events (TDEs) or active galactic nuclei (AGN) activity.
AI.method: Compilation and optical spectroscopic analysis of 33 ECLEs using multi-epoch data from SDSS, DESI, and other facilities. Sources were divided into variable (TDE-linked) and non-variable (AGN-linked) systems. Emission line profiles were measured and temporal evolution tracked. Line widths were used to infer characteristic radial distances assuming virial motion.
AI.result: Variable ECLEs show changing spectra where high-ionisation lines (e.g., [Fe X]-[Fe XIV]) appear and fade first, followed by [Fe VII] and brightening of [O III]. Coronal lines are emitted at intermediate radii between BLR and NLR. Positive correlations between gas distance and black hole mass exist: log(D)-log(M) slopes of 0.63±0.08 for [O III] and 0.69±0.12 for [Fe VII], consistent with Mass^0.5 dependence.
AI.conclusion: The temporal evolution in variable ECLEs reflects either a softening ionising continuum or outward propagation of the ionisation front following a TDE flare. The similar ionisation stratification in both variable and non-variable ECLEs suggests no fundamental difference in circumnuclear gas distributions between active and quiescent galactic nuclei. The mass-dependent radial scaling is consistent with photoionisation setting characteristic radii.

title: TDEs on FIRE: Illuminating the Cosmic Evolution of Tidal Disruption Rates
summary: Tidal disruption events have been extensively studied in the local universe, but their prevalence at high redshifts remains largely unexplored. Using the FIRE-2 cosmological zoom-in simulations, we compute the per-galaxy tidal disruption rate (TDR) over $z=1-10$, covering black holes from IMBHs to SMBHs. The averaged TDR rises from the early universe, peaks at $\sim 4 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{yr}^{-1}$ near $z \sim 2.5$, and declines to $\sim 10^{-5} \, \text{yr}^{-1}$ at $z=1$. The TDR correlates strongly with host galaxy star formation rate and central stellar density at all redshifts. Qualitatively, the TDR trends with the $M_{\rm BH}$ and $M_{\rm gal}$ persist from high redshift to the local universe, suggesting similar BH-galaxy scaling across cosmic time. Satellite galaxies exhibit comparably high TDRs, with their fractional contribution increasing significantly at high redshifts, highlighting their potential for probing IMBHs and early galaxy assembly. This work demonstrates that cosmological simulations offer a promising avenue for constraining the cosmic evolution of the TDR, paving the way for future comparisons with next-generation observations.

AI.tldr: Using FIRE-2 simulations, this study computes tidal disruption rates (TDR) for black holes at z=1-10, finding a peak of ~4×10⁻⁴ yr⁻¹ near z~2.5, strong correlations with star formation rate and stellar density, and significant contributions from satellite galaxies at high redshift.
AI.motivation: Tidal disruption events have been well-studied in the local universe, but their prevalence at high redshifts (z=1-10) remains largely unexplored.
AI.method: Using FIRE-2 cosmological zoom-in simulations, the per-galaxy tidal disruption rate was computed across z=1-10 for black holes ranging from IMBHs to SMBHs.
AI.result: The averaged TDR rises from the early universe, peaks at ~4×10⁻⁴ yr⁻¹ near z~2.5, declines to ~10⁻⁵ yr⁻¹ at z=1; strongly correlates with host galaxy SFR and central stellar density; satellite galaxies show comparably high TDRs with increasing fractional contribution at high redshift.
AI.conclusion: Cosmological simulations offer a promising avenue for constraining the cosmic evolution of the TDR, paving the way for future comparisons with next-generation observations, and satellite galaxies at high redshift provide potential for probing IMBHs and early galaxy assembly.

title: The Origin of Da Scaling: Suppressed Cooling in Fast-Cooling Mixing Layers
summary: In numerical experiments simulating Turbulent Radiative Mixing Layers (TRMLs) it is observed that as the cooling time in the mixed gas, $t_{\rm cool}$, becomes very short compared to the dynamical time of the turbulence, $t_{\rm eddy}/t_{\rm cool} \gg 1$, there is a change in the scaling behavior of the total energy radiated in the TRML as a function of this ratio, also known as the Damköhler number, ${\rm Da} \equiv t_{\rm eddy}/t_{\rm cool}$, from $\dot{E}_{\rm cool} \propto {\rm Da}^{1/2}$ to $\dot{E}_{\rm cool} \propto {\rm Da}^{1/4}$. The latter, so-called "fast-cooling," regime is of particular interest as many astrophysical mixing layers lie in this regime. We demonstrate that the origin of this change is the suppression of turbulent folding of the surface by the ram-pressure of the inflowing gas, which becomes much greater than the turbulent pressure in this regime. We present an argument that reproduces the $\dot{E}_{\rm cool} \propto {\rm Da}^{1/4}$ behavior by appealing to the suppression of the fractal structure of the interface by the ram-pressure of the inflowing gas.

AI.tldr: The paper explains a scaling transition in Turbulent Radiative Mixing Layers from $\dot{E}_{\rm cool} \propto {\rm Da}^{1/2}$ to $\dot{E}_{\rm cool} \propto {\rm Da}^{1/4}$ (where ${\rm Da}=t_{\rm eddy}/t_{\rm cool}$) by showing that in the fast-cooling regime, ram pressure from inflowing gas suppresses turbulent surface folding, reducing the fractal interface structure.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical origin of the scaling change in radiated energy from TRMLs transitioning from $\dot{E}_{\rm cool} \propto {\rm Da}^{1/2}$ to $\dot{E}_{\rm cool} \propto {\rm Da}^{1/4}$, a regime relevant to many astrophysical mixing layers.
AI.method: Analysis of numerical experiments simulating TRMLs, examining the suppression of turbulent surface folding by ram pressure in the fast-cooling regime ($t_{\rm cool} \ll t_{\rm eddy}$).
AI.result: The scaling change arises because in the fast-cooling regime, the ram pressure of inflowing gas exceeds turbulent pressure, suppressing the fractal folding of the interface, which modifies the energy scaling from $\dot{E}_{\rm cool} \propto {\rm Da}^{1/2}$ to $\dot{E}_{\rm cool} \propto {\rm Da}^{1/4}$.
AI.conclusion: The $\dot{E}_{\rm cool} \propto {\rm Da}^{1/4}$ behavior in fast-cooling TRMLs can be explained by the suppression of fractal interface structure due to ram pressure, providing a theoretical framework for understanding radiative mixing in astrophysical contexts.

title: HETDEX Public Data Release 1: Source Catalog 2 and Data Cubes from ~90 sq deg of Integral-Field Optical Spectroscopy
comment: 47 pages, 16 figures, 11 tables. All products are publicly accessible through the HETDEX data portal (https://hetdex.org/data-results/), including access to a public JupyterLab. HPSC2 is also publicly available via Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19581262). Accepted for publication in ApJS
summary: The Hobby-Eberly Telescope Dark Energy Experiment (HETDEX) is a wide-field, integral-field spectroscopic survey designed to map the large-scale distribution of Lyman-alpha emitting galaxies (LAEs) at 1.88 < z < 3.52 and constrain dark energy at cosmic noon. Using the 10-m Hobby-Eberly Telescope and the Visible Integral-Field Replicable Unit (IFU) Spectrograph, HETDEX obtains >35,000 spectra per exposure over 3500-5500 Å at R~800 with ~1.8 arcsec image quality, enabling an untargeted census of emission-line galaxies across 540 sq deg. We present HETDEX Public Data Release 1 (PDR1), comprising 431,713 IFU observations covering 86.67 sq deg of noncontiguous sky in the Spring (13h, +51°) and Fall (1.5h, 0°) fields, along with legacy regions (COSMOS, GOODS-N, NEP, SA22). PDR1 includes the HETDEX Public Source Catalog 2 (HPSC2), an expanded and reprocessed version of Mentuch Cooper et al. (2023) incorporating four additional years of data, improved quality control, and new machine learning classifiers. HPSC2 contains 426,654 LAEs, 491,411 [O II] emitters, 19,457 low-z galaxies, 18,303 active galactic nuclei, and 150,608 stars, providing coordinates, redshifts or stellar velocities, and 1D spectra for each source. Because the data cubes use local sky subtraction optimized for faint emission-line detection, they are not suited for absolute surface-brightness measurements or very extended nearby galaxies. Appendix materials include the full detection catalog, the 1.6 million-candidate LAE sample, and raw detection databases. All products are publicly accessible through the HETDEX data portal (https://hetdex.org/data-results/), including access to a public JupyterLab. HPSC2 is also publicly available via Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19581262).

AI.tldr: HETDEX PDR1 releases 431,713 IFU observations covering 86.67 sq deg, with HPSC2 containing 426,654 LAEs, 491,411 [O II] emitters, and other sources at 1.88 < z < 3.52, using the HET and VIRUS spectrograph to constrain dark energy via large-scale structure mapping.
AI.motivation: To map the large-scale distribution of Lyman-alpha emitting galaxies at cosmic noon (z~1.88-3.52) and constrain dark energy using baryon acoustic oscillations and large-scale structure measurements.
AI.method: Wide-field integral-field spectroscopic survey using the 10-m Hobby-Eberly Telescope with VIRUS (3500-5500 Å, R~800, 1.8 arcsec image quality), obtaining >35,000 spectra per exposure over 540 sq deg, with local sky subtraction optimized for faint emission-line detection.
AI.result: PDR1 includes 431,713 IFU observations over 86.67 sq deg; HPSC2 contains 426,654 LAEs, 491,411 [O II] emitters, 19,457 low-z galaxies, 18,303 AGN, and 150,608 stars with coordinates, redshifts/velocities, and 1D spectra.
AI.conclusion: Data cubes use local sky subtraction and are not suited for absolute surface-brightness measurements; all products are publicly accessible via the HETDEX data portal and Zenodo.

title: CO-dark molecular gas traced by HCO$^+$ in the diffuse interstellar medium
comment: Accepted for publication to ApJ; 20 pages, 8 figures
summary: A classic problem in the study of the interstellar medium (ISM) is the near-invisibility of molecular hydrogen (H$_2$) in cold environments. Observations of CO emission are typically used to indirectly trace H$_2$, but a significant fraction of H$_2$ in the diffuse ISM is not associated with any detectable CO emission (``CO-dark'' molecular gas). Meanwhile, observations of H$_2$ absorption trace nearly all of the H$_2$ in diffuse directions. In particular, a kinematically broad HCO$^+$ absorption signature traces extremely diffuse, CO-dark H$_2$. We have used sensitive observations of HCO$^+$, CO, and atomic hydrogen (HI) in absorption to constrain the properties of such diffuse molecular gas in five directions. The diffuse molecular gas revealed by broad HCO$^+$ absorption has a lower fraction of cold HI ($f_{\mathrm{CNM}} = 0.38^{+0.28}_{-0.27}$) and a lower fraction of hydrogen in H$_2$ ($f_{\mathrm{mol}}=0.09^{+0.06}_{-0.03}$) than gas traced by CO in the same directions. We detect almost no CO absorption from the gas traced by broad HCO$^+$ absorption. We constrain the CO abundance relative to H$_2$ to be $\lesssim10^{-6}$-$10^{-5}$ for gas traced by both broad and narrow HCO$^+$ absorption, consistent with chemical model predictions for the diffuse ISM. We further show that neither CO emission nor absorption is likely to be detected where $N(\mathrm{H_2})\lesssim\mathrm{few}\times10^{19}$ $\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ - a result of both the low CO abundance and the low H$_2$ column - while HCO$^+$ absorption is readily detected for $N(\mathrm{H_2})\gtrsim\text{few}\times10^{18}$ $\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$. These results demonstrate that even modest amounts of cold HI can bear H$_2$, providing critical constraints on the HI-to-H$_2$ transition in the ISM.

AI.tldr: This paper studies "CO-dark" molecular gas in the diffuse interstellar medium using absorption observations of HCO⁺, CO, and HI. The authors find that broad HCO⁺ absorption traces extremely diffuse H₂ with low cold HI fraction (f_CNM=0.38) and low molecular fraction (f_mol=0.09), with almost no detectable CO absorption. They constrain CO abundance relative to H₂ to ≲10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵ and show HCO⁺ absorption can detect H₂ at column densities an order of magnitude lower than CO can (N(H₂)≳few×10¹⁸ cm⁻² vs. ≳few×10¹⁹ cm⁻²), demonstrating that even modest cold HI can harbor H₂.
AI.motivation: Molecular hydrogen (H₂) is nearly invisible in cold environments, and CO observations—the standard tracer—miss a significant fraction of H₂ in the diffuse ISM ("CO-dark" molecular gas). The authors aim to probe this elusive CO-dark H₂ component and constrain its physical and chemical properties.
AI.method: Sensitive absorption-line observations of HCO⁺, CO, and HI toward five sightlines, combined with chemical modeling, to characterize diffuse molecular gas traced by broad HCO⁺ absorption features.
AI.result: 1) Gas traced by broad HCO⁺ absorption has low cold HI fraction (f_CNM=0.38) and low molecular fraction (f_mol=0.09). 2) Almost no CO absorption is detected from this gas. 3) CO abundance relative to H₂ is ≲10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵. 4) HCO⁺ absorption detects H₂ at N(H₂)≳few×10¹⁸ cm⁻², while CO requires N(H₂)≳few×10¹⁹ cm⁻².
AI.conclusion: HCO⁺ absorption is a superior tracer of diffuse, CO-dark H₂ compared to CO emission or absorption. Even modest amounts of cold HI can host H₂, providing critical empirical constraints on the HI-to-H₂ transition in the interstellar medium.

title: Bridging Roche Lobe Overflow and micro-TDEs: The Runaway Evolution of Eccentric Mass Transfer in Star-Black Hole Binaries
summary: Binary systems may undergo mass transfer while maintaining significant orbital eccentricities. Stellar-mass black holes (sBHs) can strip stars on eccentric orbits and produce micro-tidal disruption events (micro-TDEs). While previous hydrodynamical studies have focused on compact systems on the verge of disruption, the transition between self-regulated eccentric mass transfer and runaway disruption remains poorly understood. We present SPH simulations of a Sun-like star interacting with a $10\,M_\odot$ sBH across a range of initial eccentricities ($e_0=0.30$--$0.70$) and pericenter distances ($b_0=3.33$--$3.57$ in units of the tidal radius), tracking the systems for tens to over 100 orbital periods. Our results reveal that these binaries can evolve along two distinct pathways, dictated by the competition between mass-transfer-driven stellar expansion and orbital widening: (i) Runaway disruption ($b_0\lesssim 3.45$), in which mass loss at pericenter drives adiabatic expansion of the stellar envelope, leading to unstable Roche-lobe overflow and runaway disruption of the star. The stripped debris forms a thick accretion flow with hyper-Eddington accretion rates onto the sBH, potentially powering fast X-ray/UV or blue/optical transients. (ii) Stable mass transfer ($b_0\gtrsim 3.57$), in which the binary settles into a long-lived, stable mass-transfer phase lasting up to 150 orbits (the limit of our simulation), regulated by orbital expansion from pericenter mass loss. These eccentric mass-transfer events could manifest observationally as repeating, quasi-periodic flares.

AI.tldr: SPH simulations of a Sun-like star interacting with a 10 M☉ black hole across eccentricities (0.30–0.70) and pericenter distances (3.33–3.57 tidal radii) reveal two pathways: runaway disruption (b0≲3.45) producing hyper-Eddington transients, and stable mass transfer (b0≳3.57) lasting >150 orbits, which may appear as repeating quasi-periodic flares.
AI.motivation: The transition between self-regulated eccentric mass transfer and runaway disruption in binary systems with stellar-mass black holes and stars on eccentric orbits remains poorly understood, motivating a systematic hydrodynamical study across initial orbital parameters.
AI.method: SPH (Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics) simulations of a Sun-like star interacting with a 10 M☉ stellar-mass black hole, varying initial eccentricities (e0=0.30–0.70) and pericenter distances (b0=3.33–3.57 in units of the tidal radius), tracked for tens to over 100 orbital periods.
AI.result: Two distinct evolutionary pathways identified: (1) Runaway disruption (b0≲3.45) where mass-loss-driven adiabatic stellar expansion causes unstable Roche-lobe overflow, producing hyper-Eddington accretion and fast X-ray/UV or blue/optical transients; (2) Stable mass transfer (b0≳3.57) where orbital expansion regulates mass loss, lasting up to 150 orbits (simulation limit), observable as repeating quasi-periodic flares.
AI.conclusion: Eccentric mass-transfer binaries with stellar-mass black holes exhibit a bifurcation in behavior based on pericenter distance, with a critical threshold around b0≈3.45–3.57 tidal radii separating runaway disruption from stable, long-lived mass transfer, dictating distinct observational signatures.

title: A More Complex Than Expected Formation History of the Milky Way's Last Major Merger
summary: The Gaia$-$Sausage$-$Enceladus (GSE) structure, widely recognized as the most recent major accretion event experienced by our Galaxy, is traditionally interpreted as the remnant of a single ancient merger that played a significant role in building the Milky Way's inner halo. Most previous studies have characterized the GSE as a kinematically coherent population that originated from either a single progenitor or a recent infall event. Here, we present evidence for a more complex origin, based on data from the DESI and a novel unsupervised clustering algorithm, GS$^3$ Hunter. Applying this method to local halo stars near the solar neighborhood, we identify 17 structures, including known systems such as Sequoia and GSE, as well as several previously unrecognized structures/stellar streams. A more detailed analysis incorporating chronological, dynamical, and chemical dimensions reveals four distinct substructures within the GSE region, herein designated GSE$-$GSH1 (12 Gyr), GSE$-$GSH2 (10 Gyr), GSE$-$GSH3 (8 Gyr), and GSE$-$GSH4 (7 Gyr). Although all four are broadly consistent with the overall phase$-$space distribution and abundance patterns of the GSE, they display markedly distinct orbital actions and chemical abundances relative to previously reported results. This finding reveals an unprecedented level of internal complexity in the GSE's formation history and supports a scenario in which the GSE is not the remnant of a single accretion event, but rather a composite structure assembled through multiple, sequential merger episodes during the early Milky Way.

AI.tldr: The Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GSE) structure, traditionally thought to be the remnant of a single major merger event, is shown via DESI data and a new clustering algorithm (GS³ Hunter) to comprise four distinct substructures (GSE-GSH1–4) with ages from 7–12 Gyr, suggesting GSE is a composite of multiple sequential merger episodes rather than a single accretion event.
AI.motivation: To challenge the prevailing interpretation of GSE as a single merger remnant and uncover its true formation history by resolving internal complexity previously overlooked in kinematic-only analyses.
AI.method: Applied a novel unsupervised clustering algorithm (GS³ Hunter) to DESI data of local halo stars near the solar neighborhood, integrating chronological, dynamical, and chemical dimensions to identify and characterize substructures within the GSE.
AI.result: Identified 17 structures (including Sequoia, GSE, and new streams); within GSE, resolved four distinct substructures (GSE-GSH1–4) with ages of 12, 10, 8, and 7 Gyr, each showing distinct orbital actions and chemical abundances despite broad consistency with bulk GSE phase-space and abundance patterns.
AI.conclusion: GSE is not a single accretion event remnant but a composite structure assembled through multiple, sequential merger episodes in the early Milky Way, revealing an unprecedented level of internal complexity in its formation history.

title: The GALAH Survey: Neutron-Capture Elemental Abundances for 350,000 Gaia-RVS Spectra and the Chemodynamics of Accreted Structures
comment: Accepted for Publication in MNRAS; 21 Pages, 14 Figures, 8 Tables
summary: We present a comprehensive data-driven spectroscopic analysis of 357,415 red giant stars using Gaia DR3 Radial Velocity Spectrometer (RVS) spectra (8460-8700 A; $R\approx11,500$), aimed at deriving precise stellar parameters and elemental abundances (collectively referred to as stellar labels). We employ The Cannon, a generative model based on 2747 giants in common with GALAH DR4, adopting GALAH labels ($R\approx28,000$) for training. The resulting model predicts eleven stellar labels for RVS giants: effective temperature ($T_{\rm eff}$), surface gravity ($\log g$), projected rotational velocity ($v\sin i$), and abundances of [Fe/H], [Ca/Fe], [Si/Fe], [Ni/Fe], [Ti/Fe], as well as the neutron-capture elements [Zr/Fe], [Ce/Fe], and [Nd/Fe]. Building on these results, we develop a probabilistic framework to chemically identify debris from the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GSE) accretion event. A logistic regression classifier, optimised via Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling and trained on a small reference sample of GSE members and comparison stars, identifies stars with high GSE membership probabilities based solely on their chemical abundances, with the resulting candidates exhibiting distinctive abundance-ratio patterns, including [Ca/Ti], [Ti/Ce], and [Nd/Zr]. Applying independent kinematic constraints yields a robust sample of GSE candidates, demonstrating that the characteristic chemical signatures remain consistent after applying these constraints. This work demonstrates the power of data-driven analysis techniques to extract detailed chemical information from medium-resolution spectra and establishes a framework for tracing Galactic accretion events using chemical abundances.

AI.tldr: Data-driven spectroscopic analysis of 357,415 red giants from Gaia RVS spectra using The Cannon, trained on GALAH DR4, to predict 11 stellar labels. A logistic regression classifier chemically identifies Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus accretion debris, validated with kinematic constraints.
AI.motivation: To derive precise stellar parameters and elemental abundances from medium-resolution Gaia RVS spectra using data-driven methods, and to develop a chemical-based framework for identifying stars from the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus accretion event.
AI.method: Applied The Cannon (generative model) trained on 2,747 giants in common with GALAH DR4 (high-resolution) to predict 11 stellar labels from RVS spectra. Built a probabilistic logistic regression classifier with MCMC sampling to identify GSE members based on chemical abundances, then applied independent kinematic constraints for validation.
AI.result: Successfully predicted 11 stellar labels (Teff, log g, vsini, [Fe/H], [Ca/Fe], [Si/Fe], [Ni/Fe], [Ti/Fe], [Zr/Fe], [Ce/Fe], [Nd/Fe]) for 357,415 giants. The chemical classifier identified GSE candidates with distinctive abundance-ratio patterns ([Ca/Ti], [Ti/Ce], [Nd/Zr]), and these signatures remained consistent after kinematic filtering.
AI.conclusion: Data-driven techniques can extract detailed chemical information from medium-resolution spectra, and chemical abundances alone can reliably trace Galactic accretion events like GSE, establishing a framework for chemo-dynamical studies of the Milky Way's assembly history.

title: Environmental Dependence of Star Formation and Galaxy Colors around Abell 2029
summary: Environmental processes drive galaxy evolution, with the impact varying significantly across different stellar masses. We present a comprehensive environmental analysis of the galaxies within a $10^\circ \times 10^\circ$ field around A2029, utilizing high-density spectroscopic data from the DESI and SDSS surveys. We investigate the quenched fraction ($f_Q$) and red fraction ($f_{red}$) as functions of local surface density ($\log_{10} Σ_5$) across three stellar mass intervals (low-mass: $9.5 \le \log M_\star/M_\odot < 10.0$; medium-mass: $10.0 \le \log M_\star/M_\odot < 10.5$; high-mass: $\log M_\star/M_\odot \geq 10.5$ ). Our results show that, for galaxies of all masses, both star formation activity and galaxy color are strongly correlated with the local density. Although the environmental dependence of both the quenched and red fractions is somewhat weaker in low-mass galaxies than in their high-mass counterparts, the variations remain significant. This suggests that galaxy colors, even for low-mass systems, can serve as effective tracers of large-scale structure.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes environmental impacts on galaxy evolution in the A2029 field using DESI and SDSS spectroscopic data. It finds that quenched and red fractions correlate strongly with local density across all stellar masses, with somewhat weaker but still significant dependence in low-mass galaxies, suggesting colors of low-mass systems can trace large-scale structure.
AI.motivation: To understand how environmental processes drive galaxy evolution differently across stellar mass ranges, particularly whether low-mass galaxies show environmental dependence strong enough for their colors to serve as large-scale structure tracers.
AI.method: Analyzed quenched fraction (f_Q) and red fraction (f_red) as functions of local surface density (log₁₀ Σ₅) for three stellar mass intervals (low: 9.5–10.0, medium: 10.0–10.5, high: ≥10.5 log M_⋆/M_⊙) within a 10°×10° field around A2029 using high-density spectroscopy from DESI and SDSS.
AI.result: Star formation activity and galaxy color are strongly correlated with local density for all masses. Environmental dependence of quenched and red fractions is somewhat weaker in low-mass galaxies compared to high-mass ones, but variations remain significant across all mass bins.
AI.conclusion: Galaxy colors, even for low-mass systems, can serve as effective tracers of large-scale structure despite the somewhat weaker environmental dependence in low-mass galaxies.

title: ABCD: The Nuclear Structure of the Little Red Dots Revealted through Absorption, Break, Continuum, and Decrement
comment: 22 pages in the main text, 25 figures. Submitted to ApJ. Comments are welcome
summary: We present a spectroscopic analysis of 14 little red dots (LRDs) at redshifts $2.2 < z < 6.7$ using NIRSpec/MSA prism and medium-resolution grating observations, aiming to constrain the nuclear gas structure through Balmer emission-line profiles, absorption features, relative line intensities, and continuum properties. We simultaneously decompose the broad, narrow, and absorption components of ${\rm H α}$, ${\rm H β}$, and ${\rm H γ}$, and measure both integrated line ratios and velocity-resolved Balmer decrements. The narrow-line Balmer decrements are broadly consistent with Case~B recombination modified by mild dust attenuation, while the broad-line decrements are elevated to levels consistent with photoionization models of high-density gas at $n_{\rm H} \gtrsim 10^9\ {\rm cm^{-3}}$. Velocity-resolved Balmer decrements in five sources with highest signal-to-noise ratio are centrally peaked. Assuming virialized broad-line region dynamics, our model can reproduce the Balmer decrement profiles in three sources using a radial density profile with a power-law index $β<2$. The Balmer absorption lines detected in six sources yield absorber covering factors exceeding $50\%$. Sources with blueshifted absorption lines tend to have elevated narrow-line Balmer decrement, suggesting a connection between dust content and the presence of outflow. Comparing the incident luminosity inferred from broad and narrow ${\rm H α}$ emission with the continuum suggests that both the UV and optical continuum and the line emission are linked by photoionization. We propose that the distinctive spectral and continuum properties of LRDs can be explained via a viewing angle-dependent nuclear structure in which an optically thick, clumpy gaseous torus surrounds the central accretion disk, with broad-line clouds and absorbers distributed along the less-obscured polar directions.

AI.tldr: Spectroscopic analysis of 14 little red dots (LRDs) at z~2.2-6.7 using NIRSpec/MSA reveals that broad-line Balmer decrements indicate high-density gas (n_H≳10^9 cm^-3), Balmer absorption lines show covering factors >50%, and velocity-resolved profiles are centrally peaked. The paper proposes a viewing-angle-dependent model where a clumpy gaseous torus surrounds the accretion disk, with broad-line clouds and absorbers along polar directions.
AI.motivation: To constrain the nuclear gas structure of little red dots (LRDs) through comprehensive spectroscopic analysis of Balmer emission-line profiles, absorption features, line ratios, and continuum properties.
AI.method: Simultaneous decomposition of broad, narrow, and absorption components of Hα, Hβ, and Hγ; measurement of integrated and velocity-resolved Balmer decrements; photoionization modeling; comparison with virialized broad-line region dynamics assuming radial density profiles.
AI.result: Narrow-line Balmer decrements are consistent with Case B recombination with mild dust; broad-line decrements indicate high-density gas (n_H≳10^9 cm^-3); Balmer absorption lines have covering factors >50%; velocity-resolved Balmer decrements are centrally peaked; blueshifted absorption correlates with elevated narrow-line decrement; UV/optical continuum and line emission are linked by photoionization.
AI.conclusion: The spectral properties of LRDs can be explained by a viewing-angle-dependent nuclear structure: an optically thick, clumpy gaseous torus surrounding the accretion disk, with broad-line clouds and absorbers along polar directions.

title: The Extreme Rarity and Physical Properties of Low-redshift AGNs with Balmer Absorption
comment: 26 pages in the main text, 23 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: Balmer absorption lines are increasingly observed in the little red dots (LRDs) discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope, potentially tracing dense circumnuclear gas around rapidly accreting black holes. Motivated by this connection, we search for Balmer absorption using homogeneously analyzed spectra of a representative parent sample of 14,584 low-redshift ($z<0.35$) type 1 active galactic nuclei selected from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey. We identify seven sources with robust Balmer absorption (occurrence $\sim 0.05\%$) and model them with a partially covering absorber model, accounting for the spectral resolution. By fitting H$α$, H$β$, and H$γ$ simultaneously and tying their optical-depth ratios to theoretical values, we constrain optical depth at the line center ($τ_0$) and the covering factor ($C_f$). All sources with robust modeling require optically thick H$α$ absorption and typically moderate covering factors ($C_f\approx 0.2-0.6$), while the LRD analog J1025 shows $C_f \gtrsim 0.8$ consistent with recent measurements of high-redshift LRDs. The absorbers have modest velocity offsets ($\sim 150-850\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) and narrow intrinsic widths ($\sim 20-200\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$). Multi-epoch spectroscopy of three sources reveals Balmer-absorption variability on both year and month timescales. Three objects exhibit exceptionally weak Fe II emission, high Eddington ratio, and low gas-phase metallicity, an atypically rare combination of properties that might elevate the incidence of Balmer-absorption to $\sim$10%. We argue that low-metallicity conditions may suppress disk winds and help retain dense neutral gas along the line-of-sight in systems of high accretion rate.

AI.tldr: Among 14,584 low-redshift type 1 AGN, only ~0.05% show Balmer absorption lines, but under specific conditions (low metallicity, high Eddington ratio, weak Fe II), the occurrence rate can reach ~10%. These absorbers are optically thick, have modest velocity offsets, and exhibit variability. This suggests low-metallicity environments help retain dense neutral gas along the line of sight.
AI.motivation: Balmer absorption lines detected in JWST's little red dots (LRDs) may trace dense gas around accreting black holes, but their nature is poorly understood. This study aims to characterize such features using low-redshift analogs from SDSS.
AI.method: Homogeneously analyzed spectra of 14,584 low-redshift (z<0.35) type 1 AGN from SDSS. Seven sources with robust Balmer absorption were fitted with a partially covering absorber model, simultaneously constraining Hα, Hβ, Hγ optical depths and covering factors. Multi-epoch spectroscopy examined variability.
AI.result: Balmer absorption is rare (~0.05%) among type 1 AGN. Absorbers are optically thick in Hα with covering factors Cf~0.2-0.6; LRD analog J1025 shows Cf≳0.8. Velocity offsets ~150-850 km/s, intrinsic widths ~20-200 km/s. Variability seen on month/year timescales. Three objects show weak Fe II, high Eddington ratio, and low metallicity, raising absorption incidence to ~10%.
AI.conclusion: Low-metallicity conditions may suppress disk winds and help retain dense neutral gas along the line of sight in high-accretion-rate systems, explaining the otherwise rare occurrence of Balmer absorption.

title: Statistical analysis of the relative orientations between filaments and magnetic fields using Herschel and Planck data in star-forming regions
summary: Observations and simulations of the interstellar medium both suggest that magnetic fields play a key role in the formation and evolution of filaments and in the process of star formation, yet their exact role is still poorly understood. Here, we aim to statistically examine the relative orientations between filaments and magnetic fields in various star-forming regions with different physical properties and Galactic environments. We used a dedicated method, FilDReaMS, to detect and extract filaments at multiple scales, and we applied it to the 116 fields of the Herschel "Galactic Cold Cores" key project (18"-36" resolution). We then compared the filament orientations to the orientation of the plane-of-sky (PoS) magnetic field (B_PoS), inferred from Planck observations (7' resolution) using histograms of relative orientations (HROs). We find that low-N_H2 filaments tend to be roughly parallel to B_PoS at all scales, while narrow high-N_H2 filaments do not have any preferred orientations and wide high-N_H2 filaments tend to be roughly perpendicular. This change in preferred orientations occurs at a transition column density typically in the range [0.8, 8] x 10^{21} cm^{-2}, a range consistent with results of previous Planck studies. We also analyzed the HROs for filaments with embedded cores and find them to be consistent with HROs for high-N_H2 filaments. However, several fields do not follow the general trends, with a variety of behaviors that can be due to factors such as projection effects, confusion along the line of sight (LoS), or magnetic field tangling. Our analysis of projection effects shows that, statistically, preferred orientations in the PoS are indicative of true preferred orientations in 3D. Our results suggest that higher polarization fractions, p, entail weaker projection effects, consistent with the presumed link between p and the magnetic field inclination to the LoS.

AI.tldr: This study uses Herschel and Planck data to statistically analyze the relative orientations between filaments and magnetic fields across 116 star-forming regions. Low-density filaments tend to be parallel to the magnetic field, while high-density filaments tend to be perpendicular, with a transition column density around [0.8–8] × 10²¹ cm⁻². Projection effects are statistically manageable, and higher polarization fractions indicate weaker projection effects.
AI.motivation: Although magnetic fields are known to play a key role in filament formation and star formation, their exact role is still poorly understood. This study aims to statistically clarify the relationship by examining relative orientations across diverse star-forming regions.
AI.method: The study uses the FilDReaMS method to detect and extract filaments at multiple scales from 116 Herschel "Galactic Cold Cores" fields (18″–36″ resolution). Filament orientations are compared to the plane-of-sky magnetic field orientation from Planck (7′ resolution) using histograms of relative orientations (HROs).
AI.result: Low-N_H₂ filaments are roughly parallel to B_PoS across all scales; narrow high-N_H₂ filaments show no preferred orientation; wide high-N_H₂ filaments tend to be perpendicular. Transition occurs at column density [0.8–8] × 10²¹ cm⁻². HROs for filaments with embedded cores match high-N_H₂ filaments. Some fields deviate due to projection effects, LoS confusion, or magnetic field tangling. Statistical analysis shows PoS orientations indicate true 3D orientations, and higher polarization fractions correlate with weaker projection effects.
AI.conclusion: The study confirms a density-dependent shift in filament-field alignment from parallel (low density) to perpendicular (high density), consistent with previous Planck results. Projection effects are not prohibitive statistically, and polarization fraction is a useful diagnostic for projection bias.

title: Cooler Phases of the Circumgalactic Medium Are More Centrally Concentrated: Constraints from Multiphase Absorption Lines
summary: We present a systematic study of the multiphase circumgalactic medium (CGM) around galaxies and quasars, traced by Ca II $λ\lambda3934,3969$, Mg II $λ\lambda2796,2803$, and C IV $λ\lambda1548,1550$, using the Year 1 dataset from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument. These three doublets trace CGM gas across a range of temperatures, from cold to warm phases, and we employ a stacking technique to measure the corresponding absorption signals using background sources. We show that CGM structure is strongly phase-dependent: ions tracing progressively cooler gas exhibit increasingly steep radial profiles in equivalent width ($W_i$). These trends are broadly consistent with predictions from cosmological simulations, supporting a phase-stratified CGM in which cooler gas is more centrally concentrated. Specifically, halos of emission-line galaxies exhibit a strong radial transition from cool to warm gas, whereas halos of quasars show a more uniform distribution, likely regulated by active galactic nuclei feedback; in contrast, the cold gas traced by Ca II in low-redshift galaxies is tightly confined to inner regions. We further demonstrate that the radial scaling $W_i \propto D^α$ is primarily set by host stellar mass, particularly for the cool-phase medium, suggesting efficient heating processes in massive halos. By jointly leveraging multiple absorption tracers from observations and simulations, we map the CGM from cold to warm phases and place new constraints on the baryon cycle governing galaxy evolution.

AI.tldr: Using DESI Year 1 data, the authors study the multiphase CGM via Ca II, Mg II, and C IV absorption doublets. They find phase-dependent radial profiles—cooler gas is more centrally concentrated, with emission-line galaxies showing a cool-to-warm radial transition while quasar halos are more uniform due to AGN feedback. Radial scaling is primarily set by stellar mass. The results map CGM from cold to warm phases and constrain baryon cycles.
AI.motivation: To systematically characterize the multiphase (cold-to-warm) CGM structure around galaxies and quasars using stacked absorption lines from DESI, and to constrain the baryon cycle and feedback processes governing galaxy evolution.
AI.method: Stacked absorption line analysis of Ca II, Mg II, and C IV doublets from background sources in the DESI Year 1 dataset, comparing radial equivalent width profiles against cosmological simulations across different host types (emission-line galaxies, quasars, low-redshift galaxies).
AI.result: CGM structure is strongly phase-dependent: cooler gas (Ca II, Mg II) shows steeper radial profiles than warmer gas (C IV). Emission-line galaxies exhibit a cool-to-warm radial transition; quasar halos have more uniform CGM distributions, likely due to AGN feedback. Cold Ca II gas is tightly confined to inner regions. Radial scaling W_i ∝ D^α is primarily set by host stellar mass, especially for cool gas.
AI.conclusion: The multiphase CGM is phase-stratified with cooler gas more centrally concentrated. Different galaxy types show distinct CGM structures regulated by feedback. Stellar mass governs radial absorption scaling. Combined multi-tracer observations and simulations constrain the baryon cycle in galaxy evolution.

title: The open cluster NGC 2509. Stellar rotation and main sequence turnoff extension from FLAMES spectroscopy
summary: NGC 2509 is a distant (~2.5 kpc) and little-studied open cluster located in the third Galactic quadrant. It is a moderately old cluster, whose age has not yet been precisely determined. The main-sequence stars in NGC 2509 follow a narrow distribution in the color-magnitude diagram, unlike other clusters of similar age. In addition, its chemical composition has never been investigated. To address these issues and characterize the cluster we performed moderate- and high-resolution spectroscopy with FLAMES@VLT of 132 stars, both dwarfs and giants, which represents a significant fraction (~73%) of likely members. We provide atmospheric stellar parameters and, for the first time, chemical abundances for 21 species with atomic numbers up to 60. In our analysis we followed two different methodologies, both of which will be used for the incoming WEAVE stellar surveys. We find an average radial velocity for NGC 2509 of 58.6+-1.3 km\s and a mild supersolar metallicity ([Fe/H]~0.1 dex). This value is slightly higher than expected according to its galactocentric distance, but still compatible with the Galactic gradient. From the lithium content of the dwarfs and the isochrone-fitting method we obtain an age for NGC 2509 of 1.26+-0.3 Gyr. The reddening across the cluster field is negligible (A_V=0.25+-0.02 mag). The cluster peculiar main sequence turnoff is due to a narrow distribution of the rotational velocities peaking at vsini~80 km/s, with little dispersion. The chemical pattern of NGC 2509 follows the Galactic trends shown by other open clusters in the Galactic thin disk.

AI.tldr: This study characterizes the distant, little-studied open cluster NGC 2509 using FLAMES@VLT spectroscopy of 132 stars (73% of likely members). The cluster has a radial velocity of 58.6±1.3 km/s, mild supersolar metallicity ([Fe/H]~0.1 dex), an age of 1.26±0.3 Gyr, negligible reddening (A_V=0.25±0.02 mag), and chemical abundances for 21 species. The narrow main-sequence turnoff is attributed to a tight distribution of rotational velocities peaking at vsini~80 km/s. The chemical pattern aligns with Galactic thin disk trends.
AI.motivation: NGC 2509 is a distant (~2.5 kpc) open cluster in the third Galactic quadrant whose age has not been precisely determined, whose chemical composition has never been investigated, and whose main-sequence stars exhibit an unusually narrow color-magnitude distribution compared to similar-age clusters.
AI.method: Moderate- and high-resolution spectroscopy with FLAMES@VLT of 132 stars (dwarfs and giants, ~73% of likely members). Two different analysis methodologies were employed, both designed for future WEAVE stellar surveys. Atmospheric parameters and abundances for 21 species (atomic numbers up to Z=60) were derived. Age was determined via lithium content in dwarfs and isochrone fitting.
AI.result: Radial velocity: 58.6±1.3 km/s. Metallicity: [Fe/H]~0.1 dex (mild supersolar, slightly above Galactic gradient expectation but compatible). Age: 1.26±0.3 Gyr. Reddening: A_V=0.25±0.02 mag (negligible). Rotational velocities peak at vsini~80 km/s with little dispersion, explaining the narrow main-sequence turnoff. Chemical abundances for 21 species follow Galactic thin disk trends.
AI.conclusion: NGC 2509 is a moderately old (1.26 Gyr) open cluster with mild supersolar metallicity and negligible reddening. Its peculiar narrow main-sequence turnoff is caused by a tight distribution of rotational velocities. The cluster's chemical composition is consistent with the Galactic thin disk. The two analysis methodologies are validated for upcoming WEAVE surveys.

title: New Measurements of Distances to Galaxies in the NGC 1052 Field with the Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes: Testing the Bullet-Dwarf Origin of the Trail
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures; Accepted for publication in ApJ Letters
summary: NGC 1052-DF2 and DF4 are two ultra-diffuse galaxies deficient in dark matter (DM), and reported as part of a remarkable linear trail of dwarf galaxies in the NGC 1052 field. Recently, NGC 1052-DF9 has been identified as the third galaxy missing DM along the trail. This structure may have been formed in a high-velocity head-on collision between two gas-rich dwarfs, known as the "bullet-dwarf" scenario. However, the trail overlaps in projection with a foreground system, the NGC 1035 group at $\sim13$ Mpc, raising suspicions that the trail is an artifact of this superposition. DF2 and DF4 have been found to be at distances of $21.7\pm1.2$ and $20.0\pm1.6$ Mpc, respectively, using the tip of the red giant branch (TRGB) method with deep Hubble Space Telescope (HST) imaging, but the distances to other trail dwarfs remain unknown.
