In this Letter, we use HST imaging to obtain surface brightness fluctuation (SBF) distance estimates for eight candidate trail dwarfs, as well as for the giant galaxies NGC 1052 and NGC 1035. We find that the dwarfs are all at $\sim$20 Mpc, and are not associated with the foreground NGC 1035 group. However, for DF2, we derive an SBF distance of $17.7\pm1.4$ Mpc, inconsistent with the published HST TGRB distance ($21.7\pm1.2$ Mpc). Meanwhile, James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations of DF2 offer a second, and potentially more accurate, TRGB distance of $17.6\pm0.6$ Mpc. While this value matches our SBF result, it is clear that uniform JWST imaging of the remaining trail dwarfs is critically needed.

AI.tldr: Using HST surface brightness fluctuation (SBF) distances, this study confirms that eight candidate dwarf galaxies in the NGC 1052 trail are at ~20 Mpc and not associated with the foreground NGC 1035 group. However, for DF2, the SBF distance (17.7±1.4 Mpc) conflicts with the published TRGB distance (21.7±1.2 Mpc), but matches a new JWST TRGB distance (17.6±0.6 Mpc), highlighting the need for uniform JWST imaging across all trail dwarfs.
AI.motivation: To resolve whether the NGC 1052 trail is a real physical structure (possibly formed by a "bullet-dwarf" collision) or an artifact of projection overlap with the foreground NGC 1035 group, by obtaining precise distance measurements for candidate trail dwarfs.
AI.method: Surface brightness fluctuation (SBF) distance estimates using HST imaging for eight candidate trail dwarfs, plus NGC 1052 and NGC 1035; comparison with existing TRGB distances from HST and new JWST observations for DF2.
AI.result: All eight dwarf candidates are at ~20 Mpc, not associated with NGC 1035 group. DF2 SBF distance (17.7±1.4 Mpc) disagrees with HST TRGB (21.7±1.2 Mpc) but agrees with JWST TRGB (17.6±0.6 Mpc).
AI.conclusion: The NGC 1052 trail is a real physical structure at ~20 Mpc, not a projection artifact. However, lingering distance discrepancies for DF2 demonstrate that uniform JWST imaging of all trail dwarfs is critically needed to obtain consistent, accurate distances.

title: SMUGGLE-Ring: Evolutionary link between nuclear star cluster and nuclear disk
comment: 7 pages, 7 figures, submitted to A&A Letter
summary: We present a high-resolution hydrodynamical simulation of the formation and evolution of nuclear structures in a Milky Way-mass galaxy using the SMUGGLE multiphase ISM and stellar feedback model. The system naturally develops a bar of length $\approx5$ kpc in isolation, driving sustained gas inflows toward the center that lead to the formation of a nuclear stellar disk (NSD) and a nuclear star cluster (NSC). By considering only stars born after bar formation, we cleanly isolate the nuclear structures and recover a clear inside-out growth of the NSD. Consistent with observational studies, we find that stellar feedback induces repeated shocks that regulate the size of the nuclear gas disk and drive gas from its outer edge toward the NSC region. Over time, the NSD and NSC share similar mass growth and star formation histories, except during accretion of a massive star cluster with mass $\approx 3\times 10^{7}\Msun$, comparable to the most massive cluster observed near the NSC of NGC 4654. Our results suggest that both the evolutionary timescale of the bar (and thus of the NSD) and the accretion history of star clusters are essential for obtaining tighter scaling relations among nuclear structures and their host galaxies. Finally, our results favor a lower bulge mass for the Milky Way than in our model ($B/D\approx 0.045$) to explain the compact size of its nuclear disk.

AI.tldr: A high-resolution hydrodynamical simulation of a Milky Way-mass galaxy shows that bar-driven gas inflows form a nuclear stellar disk (NSD) and nuclear star cluster (NSC), with inside-out growth, feedback-regulated gas disk size, and similar mass growth histories, except during massive cluster accretion events. Results suggest bar timescale and cluster accretion history are key for scaling relations, and favor a lower Milky Way bulge mass (B/D ≈ 0.045) to explain its compact nuclear disk.
AI.motivation: To understand the formation and evolution of nuclear structures (NSD and NSC) in Milky Way-mass galaxies via high-resolution simulations with realistic multiphase ISM and stellar feedback.
AI.method: High-resolution hydrodynamical simulation using the SMUGGLE multiphase ISM and stellar feedback model, tracking a Milky Way-mass galaxy in isolation with bar formation driving gas inflows.
AI.result: A bar (~5 kpc) forms, driving gas inflows that produce an NSD and NSC. Nuclear structures show inside-out growth, feedback regulates the nuclear gas disk size, and NSD/NSC share similar growth histories except during accretion of a massive (~3×10⁷ M☉) star cluster. The Milky Way likely requires a lower bulge-to-disk ratio (~0.045) than the model predicts.
AI.conclusion: Both bar evolutionary timescale and star cluster accretion history are critical for understanding scaling relations of nuclear structures; the Milky Way's compact nuclear disk suggests a lower bulge mass than simulated.

title: Dynamics and detectability of long-lived non-accretion phases for massive black hole binaries in cold, thermally regulating disks
summary: We investigate whether the non-accreting phases found in thin, locally isothermal circumbinary disks survive when the disk thermodynamics are evolved self-consistently. We present grid-based hydrodynamics simulations of circumbinary accretion with an energy equation that includes viscous and hydrodynamic heating coupled to radiative blackbody cooling in the high-Mach number regime. We find that, although gas accumulates and heats at the far edge of the circumbinary cavity, the regions that launch accretion streams remain comparatively cold, leading to potentially long-lived suppression of the binary accretion rate as the large-scale feeding rate is reduced towards the Eddington limit. This runaway non-accretion problem, however, is weakened relative to locally isothermal solutions. Despite their low accretion rates, binaries interacting with disks in a non-accreting phase can remain sufficiently luminous and variable at optical and near-infrared frequencies to be detectable in upcoming wide-field surveys like LSST and the Roman Space Telescope. Because of the effective truncation of the surrounding disk, though, such systems are comparatively faint in high energy, photo-ionizing emission, and may therefore appear as intrinsically X-ray-weak AGN with weak or absent emission line features. We additionally suggest an update to grid-based sink prescriptions for approximating mass loss across an unresolved horizon when including an energy conservation equation.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether non-accreting phases in circumbinary disks persist under self-consistent thermodynamics. Using grid-based hydrodynamics with an energy equation including viscous/heating and radiative cooling, the authors find that gas accumulates at the cavity edge but accretion streams remain cool, suppressing binary accretion rates. Despite low accretion, binaries remain detectable in optical/NIR surveys like LSST and Roman, but appear X-ray weak due to disk truncation. The paper also proposes an updated sink prescription for energy-conserving simulations.
AI.motivation: To determine if non-accreting phases observed in locally isothermal circumbinary disk simulations survive when disk thermodynamics are evolved self-consistently, rather than prescribed.
AI.method: Grid-based hydrodynamics simulations of circumbinary accretion incorporating an energy equation with viscous heating, hydrodynamic heating, and radiative blackbody cooling in the high-Mach number regime.
AI.result: Non-accreting phases persist but are weakened compared to locally isothermal solutions. Gas heats at the cavity edge but accretion streams remain cold, leading to long-lived accretion suppression as the feeding rate approaches the Eddington limit.
AI.conclusion: Binaries in non-accreting phases remain detectable in optical/NIR surveys but appear X-ray weak with weak emission lines. An updated grid-based sink prescription for energy-conserving simulations is suggested.

title: Galactic absorption measured by X-ray observations of clusters of galaxies at the low Galactic latitude
summary: The amount of the interstellar gas in the Galaxy has been conventionally estimated through observations at various wavelengths. The estimation of the total hydrogen column density (N_H) depends on assumptions such as temperature. The X-ray absorption process is the photoelectric absorption, which depends on the number of atoms to encounter X-ray photons, and hence X-ray observations would be able to derive the N_H values independently on the condition of the interstellar matter. We measured the Galactic absorption using clusters of galaxies at the low Galactic latitude. Comparing the observed N_H with the calculated N_H} values from HI and CO intensities indicates that the observed values are systematically larger than the calculated values. The observed $N_{\rm H}$ values at high Galactic latitude (N_H<10^{22} cm^{-2}) are comparable to those estimated from N_HI} and optical reddening values using the method by Willingale et al. (2013, MNRAS, 431, 394), but the values near to the Galactic plane (N_H >10^{22} cm^{-2}) are larger than the estimated ones. The dust optical depth at 353 GHz, tau_{353}, and the observed N_H values are expressed by a linear function of N_H=(1.01-1.59)x10^{26} tau_{353} cm^{-2} even at N_H >10^{23} cm^{-2}. We also confirmed a linear correlation between the optical reddening, E(B-V), and the N_H values expressed by N_H=(6.3-9.5)x10^{21} E(B-V) cm^{-2}. This work is an additional and independent test of the relation among the amount of interstellar gas, the optical depth, and the optical reddening.

AI.tldr: This paper measures Galactic X-ray absorption using galaxy clusters to estimate total hydrogen column density (N_H) at low Galactic latitudes, finding that observed N_H values are systematically larger than those calculated from HI and CO intensities, especially near the Galactic plane (N_H >10^22 cm^-2). The study establishes linear relations between N_H and dust optical depth at 353 GHz and optical reddening E(B-V).
AI.motivation: Conventional estimates of interstellar gas in the Galaxy depend on assumptions such as temperature. X-ray absorption (photoelectric absorption) depends only on the number of atoms encountered, allowing N_H values to be derived independently of the condition of the interstellar matter. This work aims to measure Galactic absorption using clusters of galaxies as an independent test.
AI.method: The authors measured Galactic X-ray absorption using clusters of galaxies at low Galactic latitude. They compared observed N_H values with calculated N_H from HI and CO intensities, and also compared with estimates from N_HI, optical reddening (Willingale et al. 2013 method), dust optical depth at 353 GHz (tau_353), and E(B-V).
AI.result: Observed N_H values are systematically larger than calculated values from HI and CO. At high Galactic latitude (N_H <10^22 cm^-2), observed values are comparable to estimates; near the Galactic plane (N_H >10^22 cm^-2), observed values are larger. Linear relations: N_H = (1.01-1.59)x10^26 tau_353 cm^-2 and N_H = (6.3-9.5)x10^21 E(B-V) cm^-2.
AI.conclusion: This work provides an additional and independent test of the relation among interstellar gas amount, optical depth, and optical reddening, confirming linear correlations between N_H and both tau_353 and E(B-V).
